messages.subject: Omega hierarchical in lavaan?
parts:
Dear Yves,

first of all I want to thank you for your unbelievable work - this really is kind of a masterpiece!

Unfortunately I´m not an programming expert, so I have a question or a suggestion:
Have you thought about implementing the ECV/PUC and Omegahierarchical/Omegasubscale as reported on p. 687-691 in the new article from Steven Reise: 
The Rediscovery of Bifactor Measurement Models; Multivariate Behavioral Research, Volume 47, Issue 5, 2012
http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00273171.2012.715555

Maybe this could be helpful also for other users.
Anyway thank you very much for your package!

Best,

Pete

messages.author: d9ced0277ffec420
messages.subject: Re: Omega hierarchical in lavaan?
parts:
To the best of my knowledge, lavaan only used the Delta/marginal parameterization for categorical endogenous variables, which constrains the indicators' error variance to 1 (estimating the underlying variable's variance instead), thus making e1-e30 "non-free". You'll have to pretend your indicators are continuous for the syntax to work; in such cases, you might want to estimate the polychoric correlations first, and use them as input into lavaan.

Best,

Alex

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Omega hierarchical in lavaan?
parts:
On 01/28/2013 04:36 PM, Alexander Beaujean wrote:
> To the best of my knowledge, lavaan only used the Delta/marginal
> parameterization for categorical endogenous variables, which constrains
> the indicators' error variance to 1 (estimating the underlying
> variable's variance instead), thus making e1-e30 "non-free".

Just to clarify: lavaan uses the 'delta' parameterization indeed (this
is Mplus parlance). It means that the residual variances of the manifest
categorical variables are not free. They are not fixed to 1 either. They
are in fact a function of other parameter values.

Soon, the so-called 'theta' parameterization (again, Mplus parlance)
will be available too. Here, the residual variances are free, while some
other parameters are fixed. I'm considering other parameterizations too.

Yves.

One reference is:

Muth�n, B. (1978). Contributions to factor analysis of dichotomous
variables. Psychometrika, 43, 551-560.
(www.statmodel.com/download/ContributionsToFactorAnalysis.pdf)

Equation 4 (page 554) shows how the (diagonal) elements of 'Psi'
(corresponding with the residual variances of the observed variables)
are a function of other model parameters.

Yves.
